audit_findings.title: Acquisition-enabled growth may be modeled without its capital cost
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed growth uplift versus bear: $1,729 million in base equity value and $3,009 million in bull equity value; actual acquisition-capital adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth raises future OE, but acquisition outlays required to produce that growth would reduce distributable OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We look to aggressively deploy capital to grow the business and to enter attractive new verticals.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates an acquisition-led capital-allocation strategy, but it does not establish that the forecast 5%-8% growth specifically requires future acquisitions. This is therefore an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated forecast error. It is material because the modeled growth accounts for $55.32-$96.26 per share above the zero-growth case and materially determines the valuation range and buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Separate historical organic and acquired OE, document the organic basis for each forecast growth rate, and rerun base and bull cases after deducting any acquisition capital required to achieve their growth.

audit_findings.title: The anchor and valued business have different operating perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 pro forma net income was $436.0 million versus $396.6 million reported, a $39.4 million difference; normalized OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor is derived mainly from the pre-QSC perimeter and only eight months of QSC, while forecast equity represents the full QSC-inclusive business.
audit_findings.evidence: The operating results, assets, liabilities, and cash flows of QSC have been included in our consolidated financial statements since the date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. The MIN rule limits credit for unobserved earnings but does not normalize the OE of the business currently owned. QSC supplied $428.6 million of FY2025 sales, and the latest nine-month filing shows AIS sales of $809.0 million and operating profit of $121.8 million; consequently, a full-perimeter anchor could materially alter value. Direction remains unknown because additional QSC earnings must be weighed against working capital, taxes, maintenance investment, interest, and integration costs.
audit_findings.action: Use the first full post-acquisition 10-K to calculate normalized QSC-inclusive OE, reconcile it to the existing $455.9 million anchor, and rerun every scenario if the anchor changes.

audit_findings.title: Retirement and deferred-compensation claims are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $84.9 million maximum stated gross exposure before deferred-compensation asset offsets, equal to $2.72 per share and 1.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net debt-like pension or deferred-compensation claim not funded through projected OE would be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant changes in actual investment returns on defined benefit plan assets, discount rates, and other factors could adversely affect our comprehensive income and the amount of contributions we are required to make to the defined benefit plans in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although the deferred-compensation liability may be partly offset by company-owned life-insurance assets. Even deducting the entire $33.3 million pension deficit plus the full $51.6 million deferred-compensation and other-postretirement balance would reduce base value by only $2.72 per share, from $241.96 to about $239.24, and cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $334.05 market price.
audit_findings.action: Quantify company-owned life-insurance assets and any tax effects, document whether normalized OE captures required benefit funding, and record the resulting net claim for bridge completeness.

audit_findings.title: Current interest burden is not explicitly reconciled to the equity-OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified; filed nine-month FY2026 interest expense was $27.0 million, interest income was $5.5 million, and net interest expense was $21.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the valuation uses equity-level OE, recurring interest expense reduces the anchor, while portfolio interest income must be removed consistently to avoid double counting cash returns.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in net interest expense was due primarily to interest incurred on our outstanding Term Loan Facility and lower interest-bearing cash and cash equivalent balances as a result of our purchase of QSC.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing reconciliation is demonstrated, but a numerical anchor error is not. Historical years included different cash and debt structures, while current borrowings have fallen and the latest quarter reported $7.8 million of gross interest expense. The record does not show how those amounts were normalized within the $455.9 million trend anchor, so either overstatement or understatement is possible and materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the anchor with gross recurring interest expense based on the latest debt balances and contractual rates, remove portfolio interest income consistently, and rerun the valuation if normalized OE differs.

audit_findings.title: Performance-unit dilution may exceed the one-for-one share count
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified; 0.3 million performance stock units were outstanding, but maximum payout multipliers were not supplied
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSU settlement would increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: For most of these grants, the actual number of performance stock units earned for these awards will be determined at the end of the related performance period based on the level of achievement of established performance thresholds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates performance-dependent settlement, but it does not establish that payouts can exceed one share per unit or specify the maximum multiplier. Thus, denominator understatement is only a possibility. The disclosed 0.3 million units provide the affected base, but materiality cannot be determined without the award caps and without identifying what the existing 31.262547 million-share denominator already includes.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the governing PSU agreements and proxy disclosures for maximum and expected payout multipliers, reconcile all awards to the latest basic share count, and rerun per-share values using the resulting diluted denominator.

audit_findings.title: The bridge assumes all cash is excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $411.9 million, equal to $13.18 per share and 5.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating or restricted cash must be excluded from the non-operating cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our significant contractual cash requirements as of August 31, 2025 primarily include principal and interest on outstanding debt, accounts payable, accrued employee compensation, operating lease liabilities, and certain purchase obligations incurred in the ordinary course of business that are enforceable and legally binding.
audit_findings.explanation: The model demonstrably adds the entire cash balance, while the distributable portion is unresolved. Nevertheless, even the extreme removal of all $411.9 million would reduce base value only to about $228.78 per share and bull value to about $269.72, both still below the $334.05 market price. The buy-below threshold would fall from $169.37 to about $160.15, so this cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating and restricted cash from seasonal working-capital requirements, covenants, and contractual commitments, then add only the residual excess cash in the bridge.
